summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 6 upside misses — DSFIR.AS +10%, ASM.AS +10%, RR.L +8%, GLE.PA +7%, HLMA.L +7%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (UMG.AS -25%, WKL.AS -9%, REN.AS -8%, MRO.L -8%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: UMG.AS (-24.57%) — Q2'26 earnings (Jul 30): subscription growth slowed to 6.7% from 7.9%, EBITDA margin fell to 20.5%; stock plunged ~25%, its biggest one-day drop ever, erasing ~€8.8B market cap. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — UMG.AS is a Euronext Amsterdam-listed large-cap media/entertainment name (Vivendi spinoff); uk-eu universe is likely built from national blue-chip indices (AEX/FTSE/DAX) or excludes the media sector, so it was never scanned.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 2026 earnings beat (6% organic sales growth vs ~3.9% est, EBITDA €466M vs €452M est) driven by double-digit Fine/Consumer Fragrances growth; guidance nudged to upper end of 2-4% range.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — DSM-Firmenich AG sits in specialty chemicals/flavors-fragrances, a sector the uk-eu universes likely don't cover, and its dual Amsterdam/SIX Swiss listing (since May 2026) may fall through country-code-based universe construction.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a market-cap/liquidity-based universe screen (independent of sector code) for uk-eu large caps, and an earnings-day override that pulls in any liquid regional name with a post-results gap ≥8% for next-day evaluation even if outside the static universe.

top_movers.catalyst: Post-earnings re-rating: Deutsche Bank/Kepler Cheuvreux upgraded to Buy, targets to €1,070-1,100, after Q2 revenue hit record €1.003B and 2026 guidance raised above €4B on AI chip-equipment demand.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — ASM.AS is a large-cap (~€40B) Dutch semiconductor-equipment maker on Euronext Amsterdam. Move was a 3-day-delayed post-earnings analyst re-rating (results reported Jul 28, initial sell-off), not a same-day earnings gap a news-reactive gate would catch.
top_movers.suggestion: Add EU semiconductor-equipment large-caps (ASM.AS, BESI.AS) to the uk-eu universe, and add a T+1..T+5 post-earnings analyst-revision scanner that flags names with ≥2 target-price upgrades within a week of reporting.

top_movers.catalyst: H1 2026 results beat: operating profit £2.53bn vs £2.37bn est, margin 22.5% (from 19.1%), FY profit guidance raised to £4.7-4.9bn from £4.0-4.2bn; Moody's/Fitch upgrades.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — RR.L is a large-cap LSE-primary-listed UK aerospace/defence industrial; the uk-eu universe likely excludes it either as a legacy screen from its 2020-23 penny-stock/distressed era never refreshed, or a listing-currency (GBp) filter favoring US ADRs.
top_movers.suggestion: Re-run universe eligibility screens quarterly on market-cap/liquidity rather than a static list, so recovered large caps like RR.L (now ~FTSE top-10 by cap) re-enter after multi-year exclusion.

top_movers.catalyst: Record Q2 2026 profit (€1.8B, ROTE 12.2%), raised FY guidance, plus a new €1.5B buyback and 23% higher interim dividend announced 2026-07-30.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — GLE.PA is a large-cap EU bank not covered by the bot's tradable list, so no filter ever got a chance to evaluate the earnings gap.
top_movers.suggestion: Add EU banking large-caps (CAC40/Euro Stoxx constituents) to the universe with an earnings-gate that releases names showing post-results gap ≥5% within 30min of open.

top_movers.catalyst: No stock-specific news today; extends a multi-week rebound from June's photonics guidance cut, boosted by data-center capex optimism after strong Amazon earnings (echoes BofA's July Buy thesis).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: HLMA.L is a ~28bn GBP FTSE 100 industrial/health-tech conglomerate, a sector/cap bucket the uk-eu universe likely excludes; also a multi-day grind-up, not a single-session gap a scanner would flag.
top_movers.suggestion: Add data-center-capex-adjacent FTSE 100 industrials (HLMA.L, photonics suppliers) to the uk-eu universe, with a correlation trigger firing when mega-cap capex names like AMZN beat and rally.

top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — Saint-Gobain is a large-cap French building-materials/industrial conglomerate; the bot's uk-eu coverage likely skews toward a narrower sector/cap list that excludes diversified industrials, so no pre-earnings signal was ever generated.
top_movers.suggestion: Add SGO.PA and peer EU industrials (market cap >€20B) to the uk-eu universe with an earnings-gate that flags names posting post-results EBITDA beats ≥3% vs consensus for next-day momentum entry.

top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — UMG.AS is a Euronext Amsterdam-listed large-cap media/entertainment name (Vivendi spinoff); uk-eu universe is likely built from national blue-chip indices (AEX/FTSE/DAX) or excludes the media sector, so it was never scanned.

top_movers.suggestion: Create a cross-listing 'AI-disruption theme' watchlist (WKL.AS, RELX.L, TRI, THMO) alongside US AI-momentum names so sector-driven mean-reversion/momentum strategies can screen EU-listed peers sharing the same catalyst.

top_movers.suggestion: Add a UK large-cap industrials/aerospace bucket (e.g. FTSE 100 ex-financials) to the universe with an earnings-day gate that flags names with intraday moves ≥7% on results day for next-session review.
